P1-FIXPOINT-SENTENCE: The dispatcher's consolidation hold re-posted a wake-up for every held lane on every call, so the event queue grew with fleet size and, because one dispatch call does not reach a fixed point, the duplicates also changed assignments. The fix, pre-registered as change 5 before any rerun row, posts one wake-up per lane and lot and repeats dispatch at the same instant until nothing changes. Every block of E40, E41 and E42 was rerun with it; the 4,052 earlier rows are archived and reproducible with the fix off, and every number in this paper is from the rerun rows. Against the archived rows with the same cell and seed (E40: 2,750 rows matched, the primary outcome moved by −0.01 h on average and 1.3 h in absolute value, at most 105 h in one run; E42: 1,170 rows matched, the primary outcome moved by −0.02 h on average and 0.3 h in absolute value, at most 6 h in one run; E41: 132 rows matched, the primary outcome moved by +0.04 h on average and 0.3 h in absolute value, at most 3 h in one run). The per-cell before/after tables are results/E40_fixpoint_before_after.csv and the E41 and E42 files beside it.
P1-BOTTOM-MAX-NAME: the relay that is always up and the full-information marketplace
P1-H3A-SENTENCE: the test could not show it. The difference was −0.84 h with a 90 % interval of −2.6 to 0.7 h, which reaches past the margin of ±1.5 h on at least one side, so the auction may be better or worse than the marketplace by more than 10 %, and the data cannot tell.
P1-H3A-VERDICT: The 90 % interval is not inside that margin, so equivalence is not shown and H3a is not supported as stated; the interval includes zero, so the auction is shown neither better nor worse than the marketplace.
P1-H3A-INTRO-CLAUSE: kept urgent cargo waiting 5.6 % less than the full-information marketplace, a difference whose 90 % interval (−17 % to +5 %) includes zero
P1-H3A-ABSTRACT-CLAUSE: came within 0.8 h of the full-information marketplace, a difference not distinguishable from zero but too wide to show equivalence
P1-H1-60-SENTENCE: At 60 % load the same comparison cut the wait by 1,077 h (95 % CI 984 to 1,175 h, n = 30, p < 0.001), so H1's second half, that pooling helps at 60 % load too, is supported (Table 7; the 60 % rows lie outside the Holm family of Section 4.5).
P1-H4-60-SENTENCE: At 60 % load the linear model cut the wait by 31.5 h (95 % CI 25.2 to 38.2 h) and the network's difference, −1.3 h (95 % CI −6.0 to 3.1 h), includes zero (n = 30; Table 7).
P1-GROUPS-60-SENTENCE: At 60 % load the three groups stand in the same order: owners alone 1,144 to 1,630 h, the Earth-losing pooled regimes 80 to 484 h and the on-Moon regimes with the marketplace 45 to 77 h.
P1-H4-LIGHT-CLAUSE: and there the data could show neither a gain nor its absence: the gain's interval (−0.1 to 2.2 h) includes zero and reaches past the ±2 % margin
P1-LIN-WEIGHTS-SENTENCE: The largest weights lower the bid, and so favour the item, for the planned hours of the job (+1.93 h per unit, the feature scaled by 1/3), the load as a share of capacity (+1.28 h per unit) and the number of robots heard (+1.04 h per unit), and raise it for the slack to the item's target time (−1.96 h per unit, the feature scaled by 1/10), the hours to drive to the pad (−1.41 h per unit) and the battery's state of charge (−1.39 h per unit); the other weights in each direction are smaller than these.
P1-SEEDS-ADDED: No seeds were added: every cell holds the 30 seeds of the design (and the 50 runs of the second block where it applies). The rule was not applied to H3a's comparison, whose 90 % half-width of 1.64 h exceeds 10 % of the marketplace mean (1.49 h); by the rule ten more seeds should have been run for it. We report the equivalence test as it stands rather than extend the sample after seeing the result (Section 7).
P1-E41-LOSS-SENTENCE: With no message loss the four on-Moon regimes kept urgent cargo waiting 14.6 h (the elected leader), 14.3 h (the auction), 13.8 h (the learned network bids) and 10.8 h (the learned linear bids), against 14.9 h for the full-information marketplace on the same seeds; the learned linear bids lay below it by 4.2 h (2.7 to 5.7 h) and the others did not differ from it. Raising the loss to 0.40 added 1.0 h (−0.4 to 2.7 h) for the elected leader, 3.9 h (2.0 to 5.9 h) for the auction, 3.7 h (2.3 to 5.3 h) for the learned network bids and 4.3 h (2.4 to 6.4 h) for the learned linear bids, that is 0.18, 0.67, 0.67 and 1.00 % of the loss-free wait per point of loss, against about 0.3 % of makespan per point for the best allocators in Lott and Honary's benchmark [11]. The auction and the learned network bids rose above the marketplace at loss 0.40 (one-sided 95 % lower bound of the paired difference above zero); the elected leader and the learned linear bids stayed level with or below it through loss 0.40. Bursty loss at a mean rate of 0.25, against steady loss at the same rate, cut the wait of the auction by 1.4 h (95 % CI 0.4 to 2.4 h) and cut the wait of the learned linear bids by 1.2 h (95 % CI 0.4 to 2.2 h) and left the others within their intervals of zero.
P1-E41-DEPTH-SENTENCE: Bundles of up to five jobs hurt the auction: against depth 1, depth 5 raised the urgent wait by 6.0 h (95 % CI 4.4 to 7.8 h) at loss 0.25 and raised it by 10.0 h (95 % CI 7.7 to 12.6 h) at loss 0.40, and depth 2 raised it by 3.7 h (95 % CI 1.8 to 5.6 h) at loss 0.25 and raised it by 5.0 h (95 % CI 2.3 to 7.6 h) at loss 0.40. Stale claims, bids on items that another robot had already taken by the time the bundle was accepted, rose from 0 to 314 per year at depth 5 and loss 0.40. H3b, that depth 5 is worse than depth 1 at loss 0.25 to 0.40, is supported. For the learned bids at loss 0.40, depth 5 raised the wait of the learned network bids by 9.8 h (95 % CI 7.6 to 12.0 h) and raised the wait of the learned linear bids by 8.7 h (95 % CI 6.4 to 11.1 h).
P1-E41-RANGE-SENTENCE: Radio range mattered less than loss: against the default 5 km range, a 2 km range lowered the auction's urgent wait by 0.1 h (95 % CI −0.2 to 0.0 h), not distinguishable from zero, a 10 km range left it unchanged on every seed and a radio that reaches every robot raised it by 1.2 h (95 % CI −0.2 to 2.7 h), not distinguishable from zero. With the lost-link rule off the wait rose by 3,267.5 h (95 % CI 3,011.7 to 3,540.4 h), and the share of robot-time out of reach of every mast went from 5.1 % to 83.1 % (809 returns to a mast per year with the rule on). A second mast at pad B raised the wait by 1.5 h (95 % CI 0.1 to 3.2 h) and cut that share from 5.1 % to 5.0 %. H3c, that the elected leader matches the auction unless the mesh partitions, was tested in ten cells by equivalence within ±10 % (90 % CI of the ratio): the leader matched the auction under loss 0 and a perfect radio; it differed under loss 0.40 (faster by 2.6 h, 95 % CI 0.7 to 4.5 h) and the lost-link rule off (faster by 871.6 h, 95 % CI 571.3 to 1,149.8 h); under loss 0.10, loss 0.25, bursty loss, a 2 km range, a 10 km range and the second mast the interval was too wide to decide either way.
P1-E41-DEPTH-CLAUSE: Bundle depth 5 made the auction worse at message loss 0.25 and 0.40 (Section 5.5)
P1-CHECKS-SENTENCE: In addition, 70 checks of the engine's phase-5 verification suite (lunarsim/vv5.py, results in results/vv_phase5.json and on the live site's verification page) bear on this paper: 54 verifications that the code does what the model says, sixteen validations against references outside the model, by Sargent's technique historical data (16), analytic (15), internal validity (13), comparison to other models (11), traces (6), extreme condition (4), degenerate tests (3), metamorphic testing (2). Deterministic identities are held to 10−9 relative or exact; stochastic checks pass when the error is within a tolerance set in advance, and a 99 % batch-means interval that misses the reference is recorded as a bias flag, not a failure; the checks ran at commit c20da61. Their outcomes are in Section 5.9.
P1-FAILED-CHECKS-SENTENCE: Of the 70 phase-5 checks of Section 3.11 tagged to this paper, 4 failed: D10 pairing A_EARTH plan_ahead (CRN pairing reduces variance against O_ORACLE (correlation's 95 % CI above zero): A_EARTH plan_ahead (E40, 10 % load, 3eq)), the condition did not hold; D10 pairing A_EARTH strict (CRN pairing reduces variance against O_ORACLE (correlation's 95 % CI above zero): A_EARTH strict (E40, 10 % load, 3eq)), the condition did not hold; D10 pairing A_MOON (CRN pairing reduces variance against O_ORACLE (correlation's 95 % CI above zero): A_MOON (E40, 10 % load, 3eq)), the condition did not hold; D10 pairing B_EARTH strict (CRN pairing reduces variance against O_ORACLE (correlation's 95 % CI above zero): B_EARTH strict (E40, 10 % load, 3eq)), the condition did not hold. The other 66 that ran passed; 1 met its tolerance with a 99 % interval that misses the reference, recorded as a bias flag: D4 class 2.
P1-PAIRING-SENTENCE: The pairing holds for demand, landings and initial faults: in the engine's phase-5 checks (D10, Section 3.11) every regime's E40 run had the same demand as the oracle's on the same seed and start year across 880 regime pairs; the per-job intervention and fault redraws are shared in draw order and diverge once the allocations differ, in every regime. Against the oracle, pairing cut the variance of the paired difference in mean delay per delivery to 0.00–0.52 of the unpaired sum for B_EARTH plan_ahead, B_EARTH_RELAY 0.8, B_EARTH_RELAY 1.0, C_AUCTION, C_LEADER, C_LEARNED_LIN, C_LEARNED_MLP, and only to 0.90–0.99 for A_EARTH plan_ahead, A_EARTH strict, A_MOON, B_EARTH strict, whose delay varies mostly between start years; their paired intervals are little narrower than unpaired ones would be, and the bootstrap over pairs includes that variation.
P1-E41-REPLICATION-SENTENCE: E41's default auction cell reran E40's auction at 30 % on the same 30 seeds and reproduced every run exactly.
P1-H6-SHARE-SENTENCE: Allowing pairs of different owners raised the share of team items delivered from 12 % to 93 % at team share 0.10 (paired difference 82 percentage points, 95 % CI 78 to 86, n = 30) and from 11 % to 96 % at team share 0.25 (paired difference 86 percentage points, 95 % CI 83 to 88, n = 30) at message loss 0.10, and the share of all items delivered by 1.7 percentage points (1.5 to 2.0) at team share 0.10 and 5.4 percentage points (3.5 to 8.5) at team share 0.25. H6's first part, registered on the share of all items at team share 0.25, is supported (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001, Table 7). The gain held at loss 0.25 and 0.40 (Table 8).
P1-H6-MEETINGS-SENTENCE: Failed meetings rose with message loss: at team share 0.25 the auction with the commit step and a 1 h timeout had on average 4.0 failed meetings per year at loss 0.10, 12.1 at 0.25 and 25.2 at 0.40. Without the commit step it had more at loss 0.25 (15.2) and more at 0.40 (35.4): paired by seed, the step cut failed meetings by 3.1 (0.6 to 5.8) at loss 0.25 and 10.2 (4.5 to 16.0) at loss 0.40, so the second part of H6, that failed meetings rise without a commit step, is supported. The step is not free: the urgent wait with it was 1.8 h (0.1 to 3.6 h) longer at loss 0.25 and 9.1 h (6.8 to 11.5 h) longer at loss 0.40, a cost that excludes zero at both losses, because a meeting that the step refuses is a lift that waits. The timeout sets the waiting without buying fewer failures: at loss 0.25 the hours robots spent waiting at meeting points were 6.5 with a 0.5 h timeout, 12.1 with 1 h and 27.7 with 2 h, while failed meetings stayed between 12.1 and 13.8. The exploratory variant in which the base computer arbitrates each meeting had no failed meetings at either loss.
P1-H6-ABSTRACT-CLAUSE: Pairs of different owners' robots lifting heavy crates raised the share of team items delivered from 12 % to 93 %; a commit step before each meeting cut failed meetings under loss, at a cost in urgent wait
